warfarin.pharmacology: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1), reducing synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X. Metabolized primarily by CYP2C9; narrow therapeutic index with high inter-patient variability (VKORC1/CYP2C9 genotype, diet, drug interactions).
warfarin.boxed_warning: Bleeding risk, which can be fatal. Regular INR monitoring required for all treated patients.
contraindications: Pregnancy (except select mechanical heart valve cases)
Recent major surgery with bleeding risk

organ_toxicity.reason: Anticoagulant mechanism directly increases bleeding risk
organ_toxicity.toxicity: Hemorrhage at any site; risk rises sharply above therapeutic INR
organ_toxicity.frequency: Daily during initiation, then per stabilization protocol; at least monthly once stable
organ_toxicity.thresholds: INR >4.5 (or above individualized target range) warrants dose review
organ_toxicity.source: FDA prescribing information; ACCP/CHEST anticoagulation guidance

organ_toxicity.reason: Rare procoagulant paradox early in therapy (protein C/S deficiency)
organ_toxicity.frequency: During initiation, especially first 3-5 days

monitoring_parameters.why: Primary marker of anticoagulation intensity and bleeding risk
monitoring_parameters.follow_up: Per stabilization protocol, then routinely (interval individualized)
monitoring_parameters.alert_threshold: Above individualized target range, or any value with active bleeding

monitoring_parameters.follow_up: Periodic, and with any bleeding symptoms

monitoring_parameters.why: Hepatic disease alters clotting factor synthesis and warfarin sensitivity

vital_signs.why: Uncontrolled hypertension increases intracranial hemorrhage risk

warfarin.renal_dosing: No specific renal dose adjustment required, but uremia can potentiate bleeding risk.
warfarin.hepatic_dosing: Hepatic impairment increases sensitivity; lower doses and closer INR monitoring typically needed.

therapeutic_drug_monitoring.target_range: INR target individualized (commonly 2.0–3.0 for most indications)
therapeutic_drug_monitoring.notes: INR is the surrogate pharmacodynamic marker used instead of a drug concentration.

amiodarone.pharmacology: Multi-channel blocker (K, Na, Ca) with alpha/beta-adrenergic blocking properties. Extremely long half-life (weeks); potent CYP3A4/CYP2C9 and P-glycoprotein inhibitor; accumulates in tissue including thyroid, lung, liver, cornea, skin.
amiodarone.boxed_warning: Pulmonary toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and proarrhythmia; use restricted to life-threatening arrhythmias for some indications.
contraindications: Severe sinus node dysfunction without pacemaker

organ_toxicity.reason: Direct cytotoxic and phospholipidosis-related lung injury, cumulative-dose related
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then annually and with new respiratory symptoms

organ_toxicity.reason: Direct hepatocellular toxicity
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then every 6 months

organ_toxicity.reason: Iodine content and direct thyroid effects
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then every 6 months

organ_toxicity.reason: QT prolongation and bradyarrhythmia risk
organ_toxicity.toxicity: Torsades de pointes (uncommon at therapeutic use), bradycardia
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then periodically and with dose changes or interacting drugs
organ_toxicity.thresholds: QTc >500 ms or marked increase from baseline

organ_toxicity.reason: Corneal microdeposits, rare optic neuropathy
monitoring_parameters: Visual symptoms; ophthalmologic exam if symptomatic
organ_toxicity.frequency: As clinically indicated

monitoring_parameters.follow_up: Periodic and with dose/interacting drug changes

amiodarone.renal_dosing: No specific renal dose adjustment; not significantly renally cleared.
amiodarone.hepatic_dosing: Use caution in hepatic impairment; consider dose reduction and closer LFT monitoring.

therapeutic_drug_monitoring.notes: Serum levels not routinely used clinically; monitoring is toxicity-organ based.

digoxin.pharmacology: Inhibits Na+/K+-ATPase, increasing intracellular calcium (positive inotrope) and vagal tone (rate control). Narrow therapeutic index; renally eliminated largely unchanged; also a P-glycoprotein substrate.

organ_toxicity.reason: Narrow therapeutic index; toxicity manifests as arrhythmia, especially with hypokalemia or elevated levels
organ_toxicity.toxicity: Any arrhythmia, classically ectopy, AV block, bidirectional VT
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then with dose changes, renal function change, or new interacting drugs
organ_toxicity.thresholds: Digoxin level above target range, especially with hypokalemia

organ_toxicity.reason: Drug is renally cleared; reduced clearance raises levels and toxicity risk
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline and periodically, more often if renal function unstable

monitoring_parameters.why: Narrow therapeutic index drug; direct toxicity marker
monitoring_parameters.follow_up: With dose change, renal change, or suspected toxicity
monitoring_parameters.alert_threshold: Above individualized target (commonly cited reference range ~0.5-2.0 ng/mL, lower targets often preferred in heart failure)

vital_signs.why: Bradycardia is an early sign of toxicity

digoxin.renal_dosing: Requires dose reduction in renal impairment; levels should be interpreted alongside current renal function.
digoxin.hepatic_dosing: No specific hepatic dose adjustment (minimal hepatic metabolism).

therapeutic_drug_monitoring.target_range: Commonly cited reference range ~0.5-2.0 ng/mL; lower end often targeted in heart failure
therapeutic_drug_monitoring.notes: Levels should be drawn ≥6-8 hours post-dose and interpreted with clinical context and electrolytes.

metformin.pharmacology: Decreases hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity. Not hepatically metabolized; eliminated renally, unchanged.
metformin.boxed_warning: Lactic acidosis — rare but serious metabolic complication, risk increases with renal impairment, sepsis, dehydration, excess alcohol, or hepatic impairment.

organ_toxicity.reason: Impaired renal clearance allows drug accumulation, raising lactic acidosis risk
monitoring_parameters: Signs of acidosis (malaise, myalgia, respiratory distress, hypothermia)
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then at least annually (more often if renal function borderline)
organ_toxicity.thresholds: eGFR <45 warrants dose reassessment; eGFR <30 contraindicated

organ_toxicity.reason: Interferes with B12 absorption over long-term use
organ_toxicity.frequency: Periodic in long-term users

monitoring_parameters.why: Determines eligibility/dose; renal impairment raises lactic acidosis risk
monitoring_parameters.follow_up: At least annually; more often if risk factors present

metformin.renal_dosing: Dose reduction required for eGFR 30-45; contraindicated below 30 mL/min/1.73m².
metformin.hepatic_dosing: Avoid in significant hepatic impairment due to lactic acidosis risk.

therapeutic_drug_monitoring.notes: Efficacy monitored via HbA1c/glucose, not drug level.

vancomycin.pharmacology: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis; used IV for systemic gram-positive infections (oral form for C. difficile only, not systemically absorbed). Renally eliminated; requires individualized dosing.

organ_toxicity.reason: Direct nephrotoxic potential, dose/exposure related, worsened by concurrent nephrotoxins
organ_toxicity.frequency: Trough/AUC monitoring per institutional protocol (commonly before 4th-5th dose at steady state, then periodically); creatinine at least every 2-3 days during therapy
organ_toxicity.thresholds: Rising creatinine or trough/AUC above target range

organ_toxicity.reason: Ototoxicity, more likely with prolonged high exposure or concurrent ototoxic drugs
monitoring_parameters: Hearing symptoms; audiometry if prolonged high-dose therapy
organ_toxicity.frequency: As clinically indicated

organ_toxicity.reason: Rare drug-induced neutropenia with prolonged courses
organ_toxicity.frequency: Weekly for prolonged therapy

monitoring_parameters.why: Guides dosing for efficacy and nephrotoxicity avoidance
monitoring_parameters.follow_up: At steady state, then per protocol and with renal function changes

monitoring_parameters.why: Detect nephrotoxicity and guide dose adjustment
monitoring_parameters.follow_up: Every 2-3 days during therapy (more often if unstable)

vital_signs.why: Rapid infusion can cause "red man syndrome"/hypotension

vancomycin.renal_dosing: Dosing individualized to renal function; requires trough or AUC-guided dosing.
vancomycin.hepatic_dosing: No specific hepatic dose adjustment (minimal hepatic metabolism).
high_risk_populations: Concurrent nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, contrast)

therapeutic_drug_monitoring.target_range: Institution-specific AUC24/MIC or trough targets (individualized by indication and protocol)
therapeutic_drug_monitoring.notes: Exact targets should follow institutional/consensus guideline protocol rather than a single fixed number.

evidence.source: IDSA/ASHP/PIDS/SIDP consensus vancomycin monitoring guidance; FDA prescribing information

lithium.pharmacology: Exact mechanism not fully defined; affects neurotransmission and intracellular signaling. Narrow therapeutic index; renally eliminated unchanged; handled by the kidney similarly to sodium (reabsorption increases with volume depletion).
lithium.boxed_warning: Lithium toxicity closely related to serum levels; requires regular monitoring.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (relative, requires great caution)

organ_toxicity.reason: Narrow therapeutic index and direct renal tubular effects with long-term use
organ_toxicity.toxicity: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, chronic tubulointerstitial changes
organ_toxicity.frequency: Level: after each dose change until stable, then every 3-6 months; renal function every 6-12 months
organ_toxicity.thresholds: Level above target range or any symptoms of toxicity
organ_toxicity.source: FDA prescribing information; APA practice guidance

organ_toxicity.reason: Interferes with thyroid hormone synthesis/release
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then every 6-12 months

organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline if risk factors present

evidence.source: FDA-approved prescribing information (Lithobid/Eskalith label); APA practice guidance

methotrexate.pharmacology: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, impairing DNA synthesis. Low-dose weekly use in rheumatologic disease vs. high-dose oncologic use have very different toxicity profiles; renally eliminated primarily.
methotrexate.boxed_warning: Only for use in appropriate indications; risk of severe toxicity (hepatotoxicity, bone marrow suppression, pulmonary toxicity, severe skin reactions); fatal overdoses have occurred, particularly from inadvertent daily (rather than weekly) dosing in non-oncologic use.

organ_toxicity.reason: Direct hepatotoxicity, cumulative-dose related with chronic low-dose use
organ_toxicity.toxicity: Transaminitis, hepatic fibrosis with long-term use
organ_toxicity.frequency: Baseline, then periodically per indication/dose (commonly every 1-3 months in chronic low-dose therapy)
organ_toxicity.source: FDA prescribing information; ACR guidance for DMARD monitoring

organ_toxicity.reason: Antifolate effect suppresses bone marrow

carbamazepine.pharmacology: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels. Strong CYP3A4 inducer (and auto-inducer); hepatically metabolized.
carbamazepine.boxed_warning: Serious dermatologic reactions (SJS/TEN), especially in patients with HLA-B*1502 allele; aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis.
contraindications: Known HLA-B*1502 allele (in at-risk populations, relative)

phenytoin.pharmacology: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels; exhibits nonlinear (saturable) hepatic metabolism, meaning small dose changes near saturation can cause disproportionate level changes.
phenytoin.boxed_warning: Rapid IV administration associated with cardiovascular collapse; not a boxed warning for oral use but nonlinear kinetics require careful monitoring.

organ_toxicity.reason: Dose/level-related CNS toxicity due to nonlinear kinetics
organ_toxicity.toxicity: Nystagmus, ataxia, sedation, confusion at high levels
organ_toxicity.frequency: After steady state, then with dose changes or breakthrough/toxicity symptoms
organ_toxicity.thresholds: Above individualized target range, especially with clinical toxicity signs

apixaban.pharmacology: Directly inhibits factor Xa, reducing thrombin generation. Partially renally eliminated (~25%); substrate of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein.
apixaban.boxed_warning: Premature discontinuation increases thrombotic risk; epidural/spinal hematoma risk with neuraxial procedures.
contraindications: Concurrent use with other anticoagulants (except during bridging, per protocol)

apixaban.renal_dosing: Dose reduction criteria based on age, weight, and serum creatinine (per labeling); avoid in severe renal impairment on dialysis per product-specific guidance.
